body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 8 models with a format search (of 297 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 25.6 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.7 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 5 of 7 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 64%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 68%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and openai-community/gpt2 (perplexity 47 → 52.5, higher is worse).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), embedding output in BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.1 dB), layernorm bias in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 34.2 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), linear output in BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (fp8_e3m4, 34.8 dB), embedding weight in BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.2 dB) and layernorm output in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 35.5 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): mul outputs end furthest from full precision, facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 keeping only -0.8 dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), softmax in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e1m6, 1.9 dB), bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e2m5, 4.0 dB), linear in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e2m5, 4.4 dB), linear in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 7.6 dB), attention in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), silu in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 10.5 dB), attention in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.1 dB) and linear in BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (fp8_e2m5, 11.2 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 4269 (74%), fp8_e1m6 1001 (17%), fp8_e3m4 527 (9.09%); 0% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where a tensor's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d weight in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.7 dB) and conv2d bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 43.2 dB).

1 missing capability keep 31 operations in 3 models (of 8 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (31 operations in 3 models). In two sections, each ranked by the MACs its gaps hold:

### Substitute proposed or evaluated (1 gap)

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 31 operations in 3 models: 31 calls (0.99% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in openai-community/gpt2 and embedding in BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5. Cost today: 0 of 31 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 31 wait for one; 6 workarounds proposed, 2 passing its check, none evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

### Found by the plan, not yet tried (0 gaps)

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 561 of 790 tensors passed between kernels (71%) in 8 models: 387 for attention heads split or merged, 155 for other reshapes, 16 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 363 operations (363 calls, 12% of all calls; 84.1 G MACs, 3.46% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 180 and linear → add (other reshapes) 58; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (88).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 561 of 790 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations with no built-in function at the store (GELU, SiLU, tanh, …) go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 383 operations in 8 models (383 calls, 12% of all calls), most often silu (210), gelu (72) and gelu_tanh (40). Their quantized accuracy: worst 10.5 dB SQNR over 383 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 13, most 58 (facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, 58 planned groups), over 8 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

0 kernels use over 80% of the 1,024-word instruction memory (IMEM) bank, of 1 kernel measured.
title: Resource limits: 383 operations limited by the LUT and up to 58 kernel launches per pass

body: Across the surveyed models, the largest measured cost is layout conversion: 525 of 742 inter-kernel tensors (71%) must be rearranged by the reading kernel — mostly for attention head splits/merges (linear→attention, linear→bmm) — affecting 339 calls (11%) holding 83.5 G MACs (3.45%), though cycles are not yet measured. Next, resource limits: 370 operations (13% of calls, mostly SiLU/GELU) must go through a 256-entry LUT with worst-case 10.5 dB SQNR, and kernel launches per pass run to a median of 13 and up to 58. Accuracy cost from NX8 8-bit formats is also significant: model outputs keep a median 26.9 dB SQNR (worst 12.7 dB), 5 of 7 measured models lose prediction metric (worst: DiT-XL-2-256 token agreement 100%→64%), and accumulated path error is worst at mul outputs in DiT-XL-2-256 (−0.8 dB). A smaller cost is the missing run-time addressing instruction, which blocks 30 embedding-lookup calls (1.02% of calls, no MACs) in 2 models with no workaround yet. Compute efficiency (MAC utilisation), cycle counts, and IMEM usage are all not yet measured.
